rules_every_option_must_honour: An order costs that character's turn, takes effect on CID'S NEXT TURN, and burns the volley he would otherwise have fired: three resources for one boolean flip (§2.5, §4.2).
Last order wins if two are issued before Cid acts; a redundant order still burns his turn (Q4, labelled tunable).
Only Tidus and Rikku own the Trigger Command (§4.2, verified: 3 sources).
At FAR only Blk Magic, Wakka's physical attack and Lancet reach; buffs, heals and items are legal because they target your own party (§4.3). Do not smooth the asymmetry.
§4.5: in phase 2 the correct play is often to do NOTHING. The interface has to make restraint legible, not just possible.

A.title: The Trigger pair lives in the command cascade, with a cost preview
plays: On Tidus's or Rikku's turn the cascade grows two extra rows, 'Pull Back' and 'Close In', tagged Trigger; on everyone else's turn they are simply not there.
The row that matches the current range is greyed and reads 'Already near' / 'Already far', so the range itself is stated in words at the only moment you can change it.
Highlighting either row raises the ivory cost slab: 'Tidus's turn now · Cid's next turn · 1 missile volley', with the three volley pips and the one you are about to forfeit hatched in blood red.
Confirming sends the order; a gold ORDER chip clamps onto Cid's CTB tile and stays there until his turn consumes it, so the queue shows what he will do instead of firing.
Doing nothing needs no widget at all: you simply never open the rows, and the cost slab never appears — restraint costs zero clicks.
A.reads_range_without_hud: Weakest of the three. With the HUD hidden you are back to reading the creature's size, which is exactly what O-4 asks about.
A.risk: Two more rows in the cascade on two characters only — an inconsistency the player meets before it is explained. The cost slab is the part most likely to feel wrong in motion rather than in a still (plan §9 R1).

B.title: A deck-side gauge the airship slides along, orders issued from the cascade
plays: A gauge stands at the left edge for the whole fight: FAR at the top, NEAR at the bottom, a gold ship glyph sitting at the state you are in.
The red hatched band at the NEAR end is the stretch where Poison Breath reaches you; it is drawn once and never explained, and it is why pulling back mid-Inhale works.

Issuing an order from the cascade drops a dashed ghost ship at the other notch and draws the pull between them, captioned 'On Cid's turn' — the gauge, not a message, is what says the order is pending.
Cid's CTB row carries the same order as a small chevron label, so the pending change is visible in the queue as well as on the gauge.
Doing nothing is legible because the gauge simply holds still: no ghost, no pull, ship at its notch — the absence of a ghost is the picture of restraint.
B.reads_range_without_hud: Strong when the HUD is on and worthless when it is off: this is the HUD answer to O-4, and it would have to be paired with option C's staging if the muted-UI bar in §12.3 is to be met.
B.risk: A second persistent gauge on a screen that already carries CTB, slabs and cascade. If Bailey wants the fight to feel like a deck and not a cockpit, this is the option that fights that.

C.title: No persistent widget: the battlefield is re-staged, and the order is a shout
plays: There is no gauge and no permanent range read; the camera is the read. NEAR is tight, warm and low, with Evrae's head over the rail and the deck in the bottom third.
FAR pulls back: more deck under your feet, cold haze, wind streaks across the plate, and Evrae reduced to a diagonal streak against open sky — you see less of it, not a smaller copy.
The Trigger rows are still where the orders are chosen, but the confirmation is a one-shot shout across the middle of the frame — 'Pull back, Cid!' — with the line 'order stands until Cid answers'.
Cid's CTB tile is left clean; the only trace of the pending order is that shout and the cloud drift, whose speed changes the instant the ship answers.
Doing nothing is the default state of the screen, which is the strongest reading of §4.5: the fight looks calm when you are playing it correctly.
C.reads_range_without_hud: This is the only option that passes §12.3's bar on its own — with every HUD element hidden the frame still says near or far.
C.risk: It leans on art that does not exist yet: the NEAR and FAR Evrae poses are both listed NEW in the plan's §6.1, and these frames fake FAR by shrinking and rotating the approved look-B painting. It also hides the cost of an order, which is the chapter's thesis — a player may never learn that a course change burned a volley.

recommendation: A for the order, C for the read — they are not exclusive. A answers 'what does this cost me' where the decision is made; C answers 'which state am I in' without the HUD. B is the one to drop if only two survive, because its gauge duplicates what C's staging gives for free.
honest_limits: Every frame composites the approved look-B Evrae painting; the FAR frames shrink and rotate it because the FAR pose is an unpainted NEW asset (plan §6.1). The FAR silhouette Bailey eventually approves will change how strongly option C reads.
The deck plating and guard rail are CSS over backdrop B, not painted geometry. Backdrop B is the approved plate; the deck the party stands on is still to be painted.
The party figures on the deck are the approved FFX character paintings rendered as foreground silhouettes, because no back-facing pose exists.
Numbers on screen (HP, MP, three volley pips) are illustrative staging, not sourced encounter data; the only mechanic claims made here are the ones cited in `sources`.
